lesson.title: It Has There
lesson.subtitle: il y a un café ('there is a café') vs il y a trois ans ('three years ago').

hook.title: Space ('There Is') and Time ('Ago') in One Three-Word Formula
hook.content: Compare the two jobs of il y a: (1) Il y a un train dans dix minutes ('There is a train in ten minutes' — existence in space). (2) Le train est parti il y a dix minutes ('The train left ten minutes ago' — elapsed time in the past)!

footnotes.title: How to tell 'there is' apart from 'ago' in one glance
footnotes.content: Before a person or object, il y a means 'there is / there are'. Before a time span alongside a past-tense verb, il y a means 'AGO'!

pattern.title: Il y a + Object = 'There is/are'; Past Verb + il y a + Time = 'Ago'
pattern.content: Contrast Present + depuis ('for X time', ongoing) with Past + il y a ('X time ago', completed).
pattern.linguist_note: Temporal il y a ('ago') grammaticalized from existential 'there is [X time elapsed since]...'.
pattern.trap_note: Don't translate 'ten minutes ago' as *dix minutes avant — put il y a right in front of the time span: il y a dix minutes!

exercises.prompt: Sort these il y a phrases into Space ('there is/are') vs. Time ('ago'):

matching_pairs.english: Il y a un bon café ici
matching_pairs.german: Space: There is a good café here

matching_pairs.english: Il y a deux gares dans la ville
matching_pairs.german: Space: There are two stations in the city

matching_pairs.english: Je suis arrivé il y a une heure
matching_pairs.german: Time: I arrived an hour ago

matching_pairs.english: Il est parti il y a cinq minutes
matching_pairs.german: Time: He left five minutes ago

matching_pairs.english: J'ai visité Lyon il y a trois ans
matching_pairs.german: Time: I visited Lyon three years ago

exercises.target_answer: Space: There is a good café here, Space: There are two stations in the city, Time: I arrived an hour ago, Time: He left five minutes ago, Time: I visited Lyon three years ago
exercises.meaning: Il y a un bon café ici, Il y a deux gares dans la ville, Je suis arrivé il y a une heure, Il est parti il y a cinq minutes, J'ai visité Lyon il y a trois ans
exercises.explanation: Before a time span in a past sentence, il y a always means 'ago'.

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word order of 'il y a trois ans' ('three years ago')?
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: it there has three years
exercises.explanation: French puts il y a BEFORE the time span, whereas English puts 'ago' AFTER it!

exercises.prompt: Contrast Topic 20 and Topic 25: 'I have lived here FOR two years' vs. 'I arrived here two years AGO':
options: J'habite ici il y a deux ans / Je suis arrivé ici depuis deux ans
J'habite ici depuis deux ans / Je suis arrivé ici il y a deux ans
J'ai habité ici depuis deux ans / J'arrive ici il y a deux ans
exercises.target_answer: J'habite ici depuis deux ans / Je suis arrivé ici il y a deux ans
exercises.meaning: Present + depuis = 'for X time (still ongoing)'; Past + il y a = 'X time ago (completed)'!
exercises.explanation: This pair is one of the most clarifying contrasts in French grammar.

exercises.prompt: Fold both noun phrases into pre-verbal French pronouns:
exercises.full_sentence: Tu donnes la lettre à ton ami
exercises.explanation: In French, both objects step in front of the verb: the direct object (la) precedes the third-person receiver (lui).

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Il y a un train qui est parti il y a dix minutes
exercises.target_answer: Il y a un train qui est parti il y a dix minutes
exercises.meaning: There is a train that left ten minutes ago
cues: qui est parti il y a dix minutes
exercises.explanation: Both jobs of il y a in a single sentence!
exercises.affirmation: You nailed both uses of il y a in one sentence!

summary.outcome: Deploy il y a both for spatial existence ('there is/are') and elapsed past time ('ago'), contrasting it with depuis.

use_example.german: Il y a dix ans, j'habitais à Lyon.
use_example.english: Ten years ago, I used to live in Lyon.

summary.takeaway: Before a time span in the past, il y a means 'ago'.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([2502] il y a Gym): see how It Has There leads directly into il y a Gym.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "There is a train that left ten minutes ago" in French:
twist.target_answer: Il y a un train qui est parti il y a dix minutes
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Il y a un train qui est parti il y a dix minutes" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of It Has There.

il_y_a.english_meaning: there is, there are; ago (with time)
il_y_a.context_phrase: Il y a un bon bistro ici.
il_y_a.context_translation: There is a good bistro here.
il_y_a.etymology_derivation: With a spatial noun it means 'there is/are'; with a time span (il y a trois jours) it means 'three days ago'!

y.context_phrase: Tu vas à Paris ? — Oui, j'y vais.
y.context_translation: Are you going to Paris? — Yes, I'm going there.
y.etymology_derivation: Replaces any place phrase introduced by à, en, dans, or chez.

avoir.etymology_derivation: Latin habēre = have. The H dropped and stayed dropped — French never pronounces its Latin H.

ans.context_translation: I'm thirty years old (I have thirty years).
ans.etymology_derivation: Latin annus — annual, anniversary. Age is something you have in French: j'ai X ans.

semaine.etymology_derivation: Latin septimāna, the seven-morning stretch. English had the same coin: sennight, seven nights — now extinct.

minute.etymology_derivation: Medieval Latin pars minuta prima ('first small part' of an hour). Feminine in French.

heure.etymology_derivation: Latin hōra. Silent H triggers elision: l'heure.

café.etymology_derivation: Turkish kahve → Italian caffè → French café. English took the same journey twice: coffee and café.

gare.etymology_derivation: Originally a river shelter where boats pulled in.
